---
title: "GeoJSON & Shapefile Validator"
date: 2026-09-01
categories: [tool, geometry]
description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile and check whether every geometry is valid under the Simple Features model — with the reason for each error and an optional automatic repair you can download. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out whether every
geometry is valid. If it isn't, the exact reason; if you want, we'll
fix it and you can download the result.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable check
using Shapely/GEOS underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/geometry-validity.html) for the actual code,
editable and explained line by line.

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-diagnose-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
import re
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.validation import explain_validity

# explain_validity() sometimes appends the failure coordinates in
# brackets (e.g. "Self-intersection[12.5 41.9]") — split that into its
# own "position" column instead of leaving it inside "reason". R's
# st_is_valid(reason = TRUE) never includes coordinates, so R rows
# simply have no position (see geometry-validity.qmd for why). Defined
# at the top level (not inside the `if gdf is not None` block below)
# so it's always available in the session for geometry-repair-py to
# reuse, even on a run where nothing was actually loaded.
POSITION_RE = re.compile(r"^(.*?)\[([-\d.]+)\s+([-\d.]+)\]$")

def diagnose(geom):
    if geom.is_valid:
        # A valid geometry has no error position, but a locator is
        # still useful — representative_point() (unlike centroid,
        # guaranteed to fall ON the geometry, not just near it) gives
        # every row a place to be found on the map, not just the
        # invalid ones.
        p = geom.representative_point()
        return True, "", f"{round(p.x, 6)} {round(p.y, 6)}"
    message = explain_validity(geom)
    m = POSITION_RE.match(message)
    if m:
        return False, m.group(1).strip(), f"{m.group(2)} {m.group(3)}"
    return False, message, ""

# No built-in fallback: if nothing is readable, gdf stays None and the
# result is an empty FeatureCollection — this cell only ever runs
# after a successful upload or "Load example" (see autoValidate() in
# the page's JS), so in practice this branch means the uploaded file
# itself failed to parse, not "nothing uploaded yet".
gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

if gdf is not None:
    if "name" not in gdf.columns:
        gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

    diagnosis = gdf.geometry.apply(diagnose)
    gdf["valid"] = diagnosis.apply(lambda t: t[0])
    gdf["reason"] = diagnosis.apply(lambda t: t[1])
    gdf["position"] = diagnosis.apply(lambda t: t[2])

    # Every other original column from the uploaded file is kept as-is
    # (only "name" was ever guaranteed above) instead of being
    # discarded. A None in one of THOSE columns — not under our
    # control — would otherwise vanish silently crossing the
    # Pyodide->JS bridge as a live cell value (None becomes undefined,
    # and JSON.stringify drops undefined-valued keys — see
    # roadmap-acquisizione.md).
    for col in gdf.columns:
        if col != "geometry":
            gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

gdf.__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}
```

```{ojs}

// The color is decided by JS, not Python — see geometry-validity.qmd
// for the full explanation of this pattern. Repair updates "valid" in
// place (same column, not a separate valid_after) so this only ever
// needs to check the one key, before or after Fix — but "valid" is
// now three-valued (true / false / the string "fixed", see
// geometry-repair-py), so the case checks for the one color that
// ISN'T green instead of the one that is: true and "fixed" both mean
// "green" here, only false means "red".
VALIDITY_PAINT = ({
  "fill-color": [
    "case",
    ["==", ["get", "valid"], false],
    "#e05252",
    "#2ea44f"
  ],
  "fill-opacity": 0.55
})
```

`make_valid()` rebuilds the geometry into an equivalent, valid form —
reuses exactly the data just diagnosed above, no new reading of the
file.

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-repair-py}
from shapely.validation import make_valid

# "reason"/"position" are deliberately left as they were at diagnose
# time, not recomputed here: they explain what WAS wrong (and where),
# which stays true and useful even after the geometry is fixed — a
# fresh diagnose() on the repaired geometry would just blank them out
# for every row that got fixed, erasing the one thing this table is
# for. Only "valid" reflects the CURRENT state, and it's three-valued
# instead of a separate "fixed" column: True (was already valid,
# untouched), False (still invalid — make_valid() failing to produce
# a valid result would be a bug in Shapely itself, not expected, but
# handled rather than assumed away), or the string "fixed" (was
# invalid, make_valid() repaired it) — WebGeoDS.Table's iconColumns
# (shared/table.js) renders that third state as a green "✓ fixed",
# visibly distinct from an always-valid row's plain "✓". VALIDITY_PAINT
# above treats "fixed" the same as true (green) on the map.
was_valid = gdf["valid"].copy()

gdf["geometry"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: make_valid(g) if not g.is_valid else g)

now_valid = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: g.is_valid)
gdf["valid"] = [
    "fixed" if (not wv) and nv else nv
    for wv, nv in zip(was_valid, now_valid)
]

# Same reasoning as geometry-diagnose-py: keep every original column,
# fillna("") so a None in one doesn't silently drop that property
# crossing the Pyodide->JS bridge.
for col in gdf.columns:
    if col != "geometry":
        gdf[col] = gdf[col].fillna("")

gdf.__geo_interface__
```

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-export-shp-py}
# Only run on demand (see downloadButton below), not on every
# diagnose/repair: writes the CURRENT gdf as an actual shapefile
# (geopandas.to_file(), confirmed to work in this Pyodide build),
# zips the resulting .shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj/.cpg in memory, and returns
# it base64-encoded — the only way to get binary bytes out of a cell
# value and into a downloadable Blob on the JS side.
import base64
import io
import os
import zipfile

gdf.to_file("/tmp/webgeods_export.shp", driver="ESRI Shapefile")

buf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for fname in sorted(os.listdir("/tmp")):
        if fname.startswith("webgeods_export."):
            with open(f"/tmp/{fname}", "rb") as f:
                z.writestr(fname.replace("webgeods_export", "result"), f.read())

base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode("ascii")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Depends on (reads) validateSucceeded, so this cell — and the button
// it returns — is recreated the moment the first automatic diagnose
// completes, switching from disabled to enabled with no interaction
// needed (see autoValidate() above).
fixButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.textContent = "🔧 Fix";
  button.disabled = !validateSucceeded;
  button.title = validateSucceeded ? "" : "Waiting for the automatic check to finish";
  button.onclick = async () => {
    button.disabled = true;
    button.classList.add("webgeods-btn-loading");
    button.textContent = "⌛ Fixing...";
    try {
      await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("geometry-repair-py").run();
    } finally {
      button.disabled = false;
      button.classList.remove("webgeods-btn-loading");
      button.textContent = "🔧 Fix";
    }
  };
  return button;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Not promoted to shared/ (still only one tool using it): a Blob +
// a temporary <a download> is enough, no library needed. If a second
// tool ends up duplicating this same function, that's the point to
// move it into a shared file, not before.
downloadBlob = (bytesOrString, filename, mimeType) => {
  window.WebGeoDS.track?.("download_clicked", { tool: "geojson-shapefile-validator", filename });
  const blob = new Blob([bytesOrString], { type: mimeType });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = filename;
  a.click();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// base64 -> raw bytes, for the shapefile export cell's return value
// (binary data can only cross the Pyodide->JS bridge as a cell value
// via a text encoding — see geometry-export-shp-py).
base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
  const binary = atob(base64Str);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Mirrors the ORIGINAL upload format instead of always exporting
// GeoJSON: "zip"/"shapefile" both mean the upload WAS a shapefile
// (just selected two different ways — see shared/upload.js's kind
// classification), so both download as a re-zipped shapefile;
// "geojson" (or the "Load example" data, or nothing loaded at all)
// stays GeoJSON.
downloadButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  button.dataset.variant = "outline";
  button.textContent = "⬇ Download";
  button.onclick = async () => {
    button.disabled = true;
    const originalText = button.textContent;
    button.textContent = "⌛ Preparing...";
    try {
      const base = WebGeoDS.Upload.baseName(uploadedFiles);
      if (uploadKind === "zip" || uploadKind === "shapefile") {
        await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("geometry-export-shp-py").run();
        const base64 = document.getElementById("geometry-export-shp-py").value;
        downloadBlob(base64ToBytes(base64), base ? `${base}-validated.zip` : "validated-shapefile.zip", "application/zip");
      } else {
        const data = sharedMap.getGeoJSON("geometry-py");
        if (data) downloadBlob(JSON.stringify(data, null, 2), base ? `${base}-validated.geojson` : "validated-geojson.geojson", "application/geo+json");
      }
    } finally {
      button.disabled = false;
      button.textContent = originalText;
    }
  };
  return button;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
validationStats = Generators.observe((change) => {
  const isInvalid = (feature) => (feature.properties ?? {}).valid === false;
  const compute = () => {
    const features = sharedMap.getGeoJSON("geometry-py")?.features ?? [];
    const total = features.length;
    const invalid = features.filter(isInvalid).length;
    change({ total, valid: total - invalid, invalid });
  };
  compute();
  const handler = (e) => {
    if (e.dataType === "source" && e.sourceDataType === "content" && e.sourceId === "geometry-py") {
      compute();
    }
  };
  sharedMap.map.on("sourcedata", handler);
  return () => sharedMap.map.off("sourcedata", handler);
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// One DOM node grouping all 4 buttons + the live status, built in JS
// rather than composed with several `${...}` markdown interpolations
// side by side — Pandoc's math-dollar parser reads adjacent `${x}
// ${y}` in the same paragraph as inline math (`$...$`) and swallows
// them (verified empirically: rendered as literal "{fixButton}" text,
// buttons never appeared). A single `${controlPanelRow}` avoids the
// ambiguity entirely. Reactive on validationStats (recreates the row,
// re-parenting the same button elements — harmless, they keep their
// click handlers/disabled state) so the status text stays live.
//
// Does NOT include the upload widget, on purpose — see the viewof
// cell right below, in the panel markdown itself, for why.
controlPanelRow = {
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.className = "webgeods-panel-row";
  row.append(loadExampleButton, fixButton, downloadButton, resetMapButton);
  const status = document.createElement("span");
  status.className = "webgeods-panel-status";
  status.textContent = `${validationStats.total} feature, ${validationStats.valid} valid, ${validationStats.invalid} invalid`;
  row.appendChild(status);
  return row;
}
```

```{ojs}
// defined physically at this exact spot in the markdown, because a

// desynced its reactivity after the panel's first reactive
// re-render). This replacement doesn't use `viewof` at all — writes
// to `mutable uploadedFiles` (defined above) from a plain onChange
// callback instead — so that whole class of problem no longer
// applies; it's placed here simply because this is where it should
// visually appear, same as every other panel element.
uploadControl = WebGeoDS.Upload.createControl({
  label: "📁 Upload",
  onChange: (files) => { mutable uploadedFiles = files; }
})
```

<style>
/* geometry-diagnose-py/geometry-repair-py are functional (the CodeCell
   engine still runs them), just not shown: this tool's whole point is
   "same engine, less prose" (see the article link below) — a code
   editor to click "Run" in would contradict that, and the buttons in
   the panel already trigger .run() on these cells programmatically.
   NOT display:none — verified empirically (Playwright, 100%
   reproducible over repeated clean runs) that display:none causes
   window.maplibregl to never become available after all 4 of
   map.js's own load retries, something display:none-on-these-divs
   alone was enough to trigger (removing just this rule made the
   failure disappear every time, 3/3 runs). Root cause not fully
   understood — most likely CodeMirror measuring a zero-size
   container blocks the main thread long enough to break the
   maplibre-gl.js <script> race described in shared/map.js's own
   loadMapLibreScript() comment. height:0 + overflow:hidden hides the
   same content without giving CodeMirror a zero-width box to choke
   on, and doesn't reproduce the failure (3/3 clean runs).

   Stays HERE, after the last {ojs} cell, not moved before the first
   one: found empirically (bisecting against the last commit) that a
   raw <style> block placed before ANY {ojs} cell in the document
   breaks Quarto's OJS runtime outright (25 "Cannot read properties of
   null" errors from quarto-ojs-runtime.js itself, even its own error
   handler crashed trying to report the original one). Originally this
   sat right before the closing note below as a Pandoc `:::` fenced
   div, which turned out to have the OPPOSITE problem — a fenced div
   immediately after a raw HTML block doesn't get parsed as a div at
   all, rendering as literal "::: {.class}" text. Fixed by writing the
   closing note as a raw HTML <div> instead of a fenced div (below) —
   that sidesteps Pandoc's div-fencing entirely, so this <style> block
   can stay right where it always was. */
#geometry-diagnose-py, #geometry-repair-py, #geometry-export-shp-py {
  height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
}
</style>
